description: How a mobile robot moves and finds its way: locomotion and motion models, probabilistic localisation, mapping, simultaneous localisation and mapping, global and local path planning, reactive obstacle avoidance, and coordination across multiple robots. Taught through browser simulations of wheeled robots moving through mapped and unmapped environments, so every algorithm is run and measured without physical hardware.
modelledOn: Thrun, Burgard and Fox, Probabilistic Robotics
Siegwart, Nourbakhsh and Scaramuzza, Introduction to Autonomous Mobile Robots
outcomes: Derive and apply motion models for wheeled robots and predict pose from control inputs.
Localise a robot in a known map with Bayesian filters including the Kalman and particle filters.
Build an occupancy grid or feature map from range data and estimate its uncertainty.
Explain and run a SLAM algorithm that maps an unknown environment while tracking the robot's pose.
Plan global paths with graph and sampling-based planners and follow them with a local controller.
Coordinate obstacle avoidance and simple cooperation across several robots sharing a space.

units.title: Mobile robots and the navigation problem
topics: Classes of mobile robot: differential drive, Ackermann, omnidirectional, legged; actuation and sensing
The navigation stack: where am I, where is everything else, how do I get there
Sources of uncertainty: slip, noise, drift, and why probabilistic reasoning is unavoidable
Sensors for navigation: wheel encoders, IMU, lidar, cameras, GNSS and their failure modes
Setting up the browser simulation of a wheeled robot and a mapped environment

units.title: Locomotion and motion models
topics: Kinematics of differential-drive and Ackermann robots; nonholonomic constraints
Dead reckoning from wheel odometry and its accumulating error
Velocity and odometry motion models with noise; sampling predicted poses
Representing pose and uncertainty: covariance ellipses and belief distributions
Calibrating a motion model against simulated ground truth

units.title: Localisation
topics: Bayesian filtering recursion: prediction and correction with a measurement model
The Kalman filter and extended Kalman filter for pose estimation
Grid and histogram localisation; the global versus local localisation problem
Monte Carlo localisation with a particle filter; resampling and particle depletion
The kidnapped-robot problem and recovery; convergence and the number of particles

units.title: Mapping
topics: Map representations: occupancy grids, feature and landmark maps, topological maps
Building an occupancy grid from range scans with an inverse sensor model
Mapping with known poses; log-odds update and clearing dynamic obstacles
Representing and visualising map uncertainty and unobserved space

units.title: Simultaneous localisation and mapping
topics: Why mapping and localisation are coupled; the full and online SLAM problems
Scan matching and the iterative closest point idea for registering range scans
Filter-based SLAM and the growth of the state; FastSLAM with particles
Graph-based SLAM: pose graphs, constraints and nonlinear optimisation
Loop closure and its effect on global consistency; detecting and correcting drift
Running a SLAM session over a simulated building and evaluating the resulting map

units.title: Path planning
topics: Configuration space, obstacles and the free space for a mobile robot
Graph search planners: grids, Dijkstra, A* and heuristics for navigation
Sampling-based planners: probabilistic roadmaps and rapidly exploring random trees
Cost maps, inflation and planning with clearance from obstacles
Smoothing and re-planning when the map changes

units.title: Obstacle avoidance and local control
topics: Reactive avoidance: potential fields, the vector field histogram and their local minima
The dynamic window approach and trajectory sampling under velocity limits
Tracking a global path with a local controller while avoiding unexpected obstacles
Handling moving obstacles such as people in a corridor
Safe behaviour under sensor dropout and intermittent power on shared campus robots

units.title: Multi-robot systems
topics: Architectures for teams: centralised, decentralised and market-based coordination
Collision avoidance between robots and shared-space deconfliction
Task allocation and formation keeping
Communication limits and consistency of a shared map across robots
Simulating a small fleet delivering across a campus map

units.title: Integrating an autonomous navigation system
topics: Combining localisation, mapping, planning and avoidance into one navigation stack
Tuning and evaluating navigation: success rate, path length, time, safety margin
Failure recovery behaviours when localisation is lost or the goal is unreachable
Capstone: an autonomous robot that maps an unknown simulated market, then navigates deliveries through it

schedule.title: Mobile robots and their sensors
schedule.exercise: Choose a robot type and sensor set for delivering parcels across a campus and write half a page on its three main failure modes.

tasks.title: Drive a simulated differential-drive robot through a given course using wheel speed commands and record the pose after each segment
Add Gaussian noise to simulated lidar, encoder and GNSS readings and plot error against distance travelled for each sensor
Compare the position drift of an encoder-only robot and an encoder plus IMU robot on a 50 m loop and choose which to trust in each segment

schedule.title: Kinematics and odometry
schedule.exercise: Derive the pose update equations for a differential-drive robot and show by hand the position after three wheel-speed commands.

tasks.title: Compute the pose of a differential-drive robot from left and right wheel speeds over 10 time steps and plot the path
Drive a robot around a 20 m square using dead reckoning and measure the loop closure error over five runs
Sample 500 predicted poses from a noisy velocity motion model and visualise how the cloud spreads over a 10 m path

schedule.title: Uncertainty and calibration
schedule.exercise: Explain with a plot why the uncertainty of a dead-reckoned pose grows faster in heading than in position.

tasks.title: Plot the covariance ellipse of a pose after 1, 5 and 20 motion steps from sampled particles and describe its shape
Estimate the wheel radius and wheelbase from simulated ground truth by minimising odometry error over three test paths
Calibrate a motion model against ground truth, then test it on a held-out path and compare errors before and after calibration

schedule.title: Bayes filters and Kalman localisation
schedule.exercise: Describe the prediction and correction steps of a Kalman filter for a robot in a corridor, using one numeric example.

tasks.title: Step a 1D histogram filter through five move and sense cycles on a corridor with three doors and record the belief after each
Implement a Kalman filter for a robot measuring range to a landmark and plot the estimate against ground truth with its 2-sigma bound
Localise a robot from an unknown start on a grid map using histogram localisation and measure the steps needed to converge on symmetric corridors

schedule.title: Particle filters
schedule.exercise: Write a short note on why a particle filter suits global localisation and how many particles you would choose.

tasks.title: Run Monte Carlo localisation with 200 particles in a mapped room and watch the cloud converge as the robot moves
Implement a resampling step and detect particle depletion by tracking the effective sample size over 100 steps
Kidnap the robot to a new location, add random particles for recovery and compare recovery time for 100, 500 and 2000 particles

schedule.title: Occupancy grid mapping
schedule.exercise: Choose a map representation for a market with moving stalls and justify it against two alternatives.

tasks.title: Convert a floor plan into an occupancy grid, a landmark map and a topological map, and compare how each answers a route question
Build an occupancy grid from 360 lidar scans using an inverse sensor model and display the resulting map against ground truth
Apply log-odds updates over 200 scans, clear cells where a person walked through, and measure map error before and after clearing

schedule.title: Scan matching and SLAM basics
schedule.exercise: Explain how a small heading error at the start leads to a badly bent map later in a long corridor.

tasks.title: Show how odometry error warps a map built from known-pose scans versus noisy-pose scans of the same room and measure the error
Align two lidar scans with an iterative closest point loop and plot the residual error over iterations
Run a FastSLAM simulation with 50 particles in a building with five landmarks and compare landmark errors with a plain filter

schedule.title: Graph SLAM and loop closure
schedule.exercise: Evaluate a SLAM map by measuring its error against ground truth, and propose two improvements for the largest error.

tasks.title: Build a pose graph from 30 odometry constraints and optimise it with least squares to reduce the error after one loop closure
Detect a loop closure when the robot returns to a known place, apply it, and measure the global map consistency before and after
Run a SLAM session in a simulated building, evaluate the map with ground truth, and tune parameters to reduce error by 30 percent

schedule.title: Path planning
schedule.exercise: Plan a route for a delivery robot across a campus map and compare the paths found by Dijkstra, A* and a sampling planner.

tasks.title: Inflate obstacles by the robot radius on a grid map and draw the free space the planner is allowed to use
Plan a path on a 30x30 grid with Dijkstra and A* using Manhattan and Euclidean heuristics, and compare the nodes expanded
Run an RRT and a probabilistic roadmap on a cluttered map and compare path length, planning time and success over 20 queries

schedule.title: Cost maps and re-planning
schedule.exercise: Tune the inflation radius and cost decay for a corridor robot, and explain what happens if you set each too small or too large.

tasks.title: Create a cost map with inflation around walls and plan a path that keeps at least 0.5 m clearance
Block a doorway during a run, trigger re-planning, and compare the detour length with the original path
Smooth a grid path with shortcutting and spline fitting, and compare length, curvature and clearance of the raw and smoothed paths

schedule.title: Obstacle avoidance
schedule.exercise: List the situations in which potential fields fail and describe the behaviour you would add to escape each.

tasks.title: Drive a robot toward a goal with a potential field, find a local minimum in a U-shaped obstacle, and describe the escape behaviour
Implement a dynamic window planner with velocity and acceleration limits and compare its trajectories on three obstacle layouts
Navigate a corridor with a person crossing the path, and tune the avoidance to give zero collisions and a delay below 5 seconds

schedule.title: Multi-robot coordination
schedule.exercise: Design a delivery task assignment for four campus robots, comparing centralised and market-based allocation by total time.

tasks.title: Allocate 10 delivery tasks to 3 robots using centralised assignment and compare the total travel time with a greedy rule
Deconflict two robots meeting at a narrow door by priority rules and show there is no deadlock over 20 random starts
Simulate a fleet of five robots delivering across a campus map, measure completion time and collisions, and improve the plan under a communication limit

schedule.title: Integrated navigation and capstone
schedule.exercise: Write a test report for the capstone robot with results across five maps and a table of failures by cause.

tasks.title: Connect localisation, planner and local avoider in one stack and complete a delivery on a given map, logging the module active at each step
Run 30 navigation trials across three maps, compute success rate, path length, time and minimum clearance, and tune one parameter to improve the worst metric
Map an unknown simulated market, then complete 10 deliveries through it with recovery from lost localisation and blocked goals
